claim_text: Non-GAAP diluted EPS was $4.74, +23% YoY.
Consensus non-GAAP EPS estimate (LSEG, as cited by financial media) was $4.24. No as-of date could be traced to a specific corroborating source.
Actual, GAAP diluted EPS was $4.81, +32% YoY.
Revenue was $90.0 billion (rounded, per company release) / $90.01 billion (unrounded, per secondary sources), +18% YoY, +17% constant currency.

Consensus revenue estimate (LSEG-linked, the pairing that appeared together in one internally consistent source) was approximately $87.61 billion. Individual citations for the broader consensus cluster ranged $87.42B-$87.67B across sources/providers; only the single internally-consistent $87.61B LSEG figure is used here, not the blended cluster. No as-of date could be traced to a specific corroborating source.
Microsoft Cloud revenue (Azure, M365 Commercial cloud, Dynamics 365 cloud, other cloud services) was $59.3 billion, +27% YoY.
Azure and other cloud services revenue grew 43% year over year, accelerating from 40% growth in the prior quarter (Q3 FY2026).
Azure's annualized revenue run rate crossed $100 billion for the first time in company history.
Intelligent Cloud segment revenue was $39.3 billion, +32% YoY (+31% constant currency).
More Personal Computing segment revenue was $12.9 billion, -4% YoY (-5% constant currency) -- the one segment that declined year over year.
Windows OEM and Devices revenue declined 7% year over year.

Xbox content and services revenue declined 10% year over year; management linked this to "necessary decisions required across our content portfolio" and separately disclosed severance and impairment charges tied to Xbox during the quarter.

Q1 FY2027 revenue guidance was $89.85B-$90.95B (implied growth 16%-17%), versus an LSEG analyst estimate of $89.66 billion cited by media -- guidance midpoint (~$90.4B) is above the pre-print consensus.

Azure growth guidance for Q1 FY2027 was "approximately 45% in constant currency," versus actual Q4 FY2026 Azure growth of 43% -- management is guiding for further acceleration, not deceleration, into the new fiscal year.

Capital expenditure guidance was "over $50 billion" for Q1 FY2027. Calendar-year 2026 capex expectations were characterized as unchanged in absolute infrastructure-investment terms, but the reported CapEx figure rises to approximately $175 billion because of a shift from finance leases to operating leases.

Microsoft disclosed a change in useful-life accounting for data centers and office buildings, extended from 15 to 25 years starting fiscal 2027, which will reduce depreciation expense. This is a new, non-trivial accounting-policy disclosure, not previously guided.
Operating margin guidance for Q1 FY2027 was "relatively flat year-over-year."

Nadella: capital expenditure demand "continues to exceed available supply"; the company "added 31 new data centers across five continents this quarter" and expects to "roughly double our overall capacity in just two years."
Hood: "roughly two-thirds of our CapEx was for short-lived assets, primarily CPUs and GPUs."

Nadella, on the More Personal Computing decline: "necessary decisions required across our content portfolio" in gaming, while asserting the company "can bring these strengths together and expect[s] to return the business to growth in fiscal 2027."
Microsoft 365 Copilot paid seats surpassed 30 million, versus "just over 20 million" in April 2026.
